def tensor_avgpool_kernel(x, pool_size):
    C, H, W = x.shape
    p = pool_size
    out_shape = (C, H // p, W // p)
    out = nl.ndarray(out_shape, dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    tile = nl.ndarray((C, H, W), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)
    
    # Compute the average over the pool window
    # Reshape to (C, H//p, p, W//p, p)
    # Then take mean over the last two dimensions
    # We'll use tile views and reductions to achieve this
    
    # Compute the number of tiles needed in each dimension
    num_h_tiles = H // p
    num_w_tiles = W // p
    
    # Allocate a tile for the result
    result_tile = nl.ndarray((C, num_h_tiles, num_w_tiles), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.psum)
    
    # Loop over each tile in the H dimension
    for h in nl.affine_range(num_h_tiles):
        # Loop over each tile in the W dimension
        for w in nl.affine_range(num_w_tiles):
            # Define the view for the current tile
            view = tile[:, h*p:(h+1)*p, w*p:(w+1)*p]
            # Sum over the pool window
            sum_tile = nl.sum(view, axis=[1, 2], keepdims=True)
            # Compute the average by scaling by 1/p^2
            avg_tile = nl.ndarray((C, 1, 1), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
            nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=avg_tile, data=sum_tile, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=1.0 / (p * p))
            # Write to the result tile
            result_tile[:, h, w] = avg_tile

    return out
